title: Drop the 30-word sentence cap, and retire every fixed number that refuses or fails without an owner ruling
why: Arbitrary static numbers fail work that is fine; the owner ruled them out.
note: R37 (owner 12:54 and 12:56 CST Nov 11, relayed by the retrospective; plan 7066904). Owner 12:54: "i thought i eliminated all STE requirements from everywhere in the repo weeks ago (along with hard limits like 30 vs 31 words etc, and instead just say keep things tight or oh ythere's too much verbiage / reptition -- given my disdain for hard arbitrary static numeric limits)"; 12:56: "A -- and im sure this 30 word thing is only one of many stale digit level hooks". Ruling: STE001 (max_words 30) stops failing; wordiness and repetition go to reviewers and judges; the lint, its action, codes and rule anchor output-write-in-ste drop "STE" (step ste-lint-rename). A read-only census (Explore Sonnet, started 12:57 CST by the retrospective) lists every fixed number that refuses or fails; each one the owner did not rule is retired or derived from measured runs. Home: decision plain-prose-lint, rewritten in place. Measured: 73 of 3561 commits on main since Nov 4 (2%) name an STE fix or a sentence split. Owner 13:10 CST (relayed): "on fixed numbers A". Census of about 45 in plan R37 (a7fb06a50), with two contradictions: merge.py 70% vs ci-job-caps 80%; bin/sim-lease load average vs machine-load-brake. Lane fixed-number-limits-census started 11:05 CST Nov 12 (coordinator 11:06 CST; owner chat 11:04 CST via the retrospective). Owner page save 12:54 CST Nov 12: item 602 a (a cap-lift end time joins the existing ask, shown in Central, any length). Item 595 none of these: "you're taking my ruling no hard fixed numbers too broadly and seriously..."; read as keep the 14-day missing-hook window, row L3 dropped with no change; R37 aims at limits that cut work off. Reopen if the owner says otherwise.
